name: Kappl
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny family village in the Paznaun Valley with over 90 historic hamlets, the Dias ski area, and stunning Verwall peaks.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kappl is situated at an elevation of 1,258 metres in the lower Paznaun Valley in the Tyrolean Oberland. Nestled between the glaciated peaks of the Samnaun Alps to the south and the rugged Verwall mountain range to the north, this municipality of approximately 2,630 residents is the second largest in the valley. A distinctive hallmark of Kappl is its historical settlement layout: more than 90 sunny hamlets and traditional clusters of farmsteads are scattered across gentle slopes high above the rushing Trisanna River. While neighbouring Ischgl is famed for its vibrant nightlife, Kappl has carefully preserved its tranquil identity as a welcoming haven for families. Sun-drenched slopes, historic mountain farmsteads, and majestic alpine vistas characterize the scenery throughout every season.

History

Kappl was first documented in 1370 under the name 'ze dem Kappel'. The village name originates from a humble chapel erected in honour of Saint Anthony the Great. Originally, Rhaeto-Romance pastoralists from the Engadin valley in Switzerland used these fertile alpine pastures during the summer months, leaving behind melodic field names such as Dias and Ulmich. During the twelfth and thirteenth centuries, settlers from the adjacent Stanzer Valley crossed high alpine passes to establish permanent settlements. The Parish Church of Saint Anthony was initially constructed in the fifteenth century and later embellished with ornate Rococo stucco and ceiling frescoes by Philipp Jakob Greil in the eighteenth century. The historic cemetery chapel features rare Baroque dance-of-death wall paintings, and nearly every hamlet preserves its own consecrated chapel.

Getting There

Travelling by car is straightforward via the Inntal Autobahn A12 and the Arlberg Expressway S16, taking the Pians/Paznaun exit. From there, the B188 Silvretta Federal Highway leads south-west for roughly 16 kilometres directly into Kappl. During the summer months, motorists can also choose the scenic Silvretta High Alpine Road from Vorarlberg. Rail passengers arrive at the Landeck-Zams long-distance railway station. Directly outside the terminal, VVT regional bus route 260 runs at frequent intervals to Kappl and onward to Ischgl. Within the Paznaun Valley, a complimentary ski and hiking bus network provides convenient local transit for guests throughout the year.

Tips

During the winter months, the Kappl ski area around the Dias Alpine pastures offers 42 kilometres of immaculate pistes reaching elevations of up to 2,690 metres. The eight-kilometre Lattenabfahrt descent, conquering more than 1,000 metres of vertical drop, is an absolute highlight. At the top station of the modern Dias gondola, families can explore the expansive 25,000-square-metre Sunny Mountain Adventure Park, featuring beginner ski carpets, sensory ponds, and play zones. Off-piste enthusiasts flock to the powdery bowls beneath Blankakopf, a regular stop on the prestigious Open Faces Freeride Series. In summer, the historic stone dairy of Alte Alpe Dias hosts an authentic alpine museum and cheese dairy. Mountain hikers can ascend to the Niederelbe alpine hut at 2,310 metres and tackle the majestic summit of the Hoher Riffler at 3,168 metres.
